text:
TOLLIVER COUNTY PUBLIC SCHOOLS
SECTION 504 ACCOMMODATION PLAN / INDIVIDUAL HEALTH PLAN (IHP)
Case No.: TCS-504-26-0417B                                  Page 1 of 3

STUDENT: STIDHAM-ROSE, WREN C.          DOB: 03/14/2015     Age: 11
Student ID: 2031447     Lunch #: 55218     Grade: 6
KY Medicaid ID: 9920417763
School: Sugar Camp Elementary School (K-8)
Physical: 2230 Left Fork of Lick Branch Rd., up Tackett Holler (third trailer past the swinging bridge)
Mailing: RR 2 Box 114-A, Cedar Knob, KY 41563
Meeting date: 09/22/2026     30-day review: Oct. 6, 2026     Annual review due: 9-22-27

ELIGIBILITY
Wren Callie Stidham-Rose ("Wrennie") was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes in August 2025 after a DKA admission, and with generalized anxiety disorder on 1/28/2026. Both conditions substantially limit endocrine function, eating, concentrating and learning. W.S.R. is eligible under Section 504. She does not require specially designed instruction at this time.

DATA REVIEWED
Scores are average to low average; the gap shows up on days with lows. On the WJ-IV (given 5/2026 at SCE) she earned Broad Reading SS 101 (53rd percentile) and Broad Math SS 88 (21st percentile). Math Fluency SS 79 (8th percentile) was her lowest score. BASC-3 parent Anxiety T-score 74 (clinically significant); teacher rating T-score 66 (at-risk). BRIEF-2 Emotional Control T = 68. Fall i-Ready Math placed her one grade level below (scale score 471).

  Assessment              Score       %ile   Range
  WJ-IV Broad Reading     SS 101      53     Average
  WJ-IV Broad Math        SS 88       21     Low Average
  WJ-IV Math Fluency      SS 79       8      Low
  BASC-3 Anxiety (Parent) T 74        --     Clin. Sig.
  BASC-3 Anxiety (Teacher) T 66       --     At-Risk
  BRIEF-2 Emot. Control   T 68        --     Elevated
  DIBELS 8 ORF            142 wcpm    61     At Benchmark

NURSE CARE PLAN
School nurse: Mrs. Loretta Branch, RN  (606) 555-0100 ext. 214  lbranch@tolliver.example.org
Devices: Dexcom G7 CGM (back of arm, changed at home every 10 days) and Omnipod 5 pump in automated mode, Humalog. Wren's CGM shares to Mom's phone and the nurse office iPad. Her phone stays on her at all times; this is not a phone-policy violation.
Target 120. Carb ratio 1 unit: 12 g. Correction 1 unit per 45 mg/dL over 150.
LOW (under 70, or under 90 with down arrows): 15 g fast carbs (4 glucose tabs or 4 oz juice), recheck in 15 minutes, repeat. Never send her to the office alone when low.
SEVERE LOW (unresponsive, seizure, cannot swallow): Baqsimi 3 mg nasal, call 911, then parent.
HIGH (over 250): check ketones. Moderate/large ketones or two readings over 300 = call parent, no PE.
Pump failure: backup Humalog pen in nurse office. Parent restocks supplies on Mondays.
Nurse time: about 20 minutes per day, including lunch carb check and bolus at 11:05.

PHYSICIAN
Dr. Anita Varghese, Pediatric Endocrinology, Levisa Valley Children's Clinic, Kettle Gap, KY
Clinic 606-555-0177 / fax 606-555-0178. MRN LV-448120. Diabetes educator: Marcy Bush, RN, CDCES.
Outside therapist: Journey Adams, LPCC, Twin Poplar Counseling (every other Thursday).

ACCOMMODATIONS
1. Unrestricted access to water, restroom, snacks and the nurse in every class, on the bus and on field trips.
2. Phone with CGM app kept on person; staff respond to CGM alarms per IHP.
3. If BG is under 70 or over 300 during a test, the test stops and she may retake it later without penalty.
4. Extended time (1.5x) on classroom tests and district assessments.
5. Timed math fact drills given untimed.
6. Break card for the calm-down space (counselor's office), up to 10 minutes.
7. Advance notice of drills and schedule changes when possible.
8. Trained adult on every field trip; bus 14 driver trained on low signs.
9. Glucose checks done privately, not in front of the class.

COUNSELING
Ms. Harmony Gayheart, school counselor: 30 minutes per week individual check-in (Tuesday flex), plus contact with outside therapist monthly.

SELF-MANAGEMENT GOALS
- By end of first semester, Wren will count carbohydrates for school lunch within 10 grams of the nurse's count on 4 of 5 days.
- Wren will use a coping strategy and return to class within 10 minutes on 80% of break-card uses.

EMERGENCY CONTACTS
1. Tasha Stidham (mother) cell 606-555-0142, work (606) 555-0119 ext. 3, tstidham82@example.com
2. Dewayne Caudill ("Dew"), stepdad, 606.555.0163
3. Earlene Stidham (Mamaw) / Arvel Stidham (Papaw), home 555-0187, landline only
4. Crystal Wells (aunt) 606-555-0151
DO NOT release to biological father, Bo Rose, per custody order 2024-CI-00318.

PARENT MEETING NOTES 09/22/2026
Present: Tasha Stidham, Dewayne Caudill, Mr. Garrett Slone (504 Coordinator/Asst. Principal, gslone@tolliver.example.org), Mrs. Branch, Mrs. Kayla Osborne (6th grade homeroom), Ms. Gayheart, Coach Colt Pratt.
Mom says most lows come after PE and on Wednesdays after 4-H goat club. Wren shows Nubian goats at the Tolliver County Fair and is the only sixth grader on a pump at SCE, which makes her self-conscious. Mamaw Earlene picks her up Thursdays. Papaw Arvel's bait shop at the mouth of Lick Branch keeps juice boxes for the bus. Tash works 2nd shift at the Cedar Knob Dollar General; text first, then call the work line. Coach Pratt will keep glucose tabs in the gym bag for basketball. Mrs. Osborne said anxiety spikes before timed math facts (see #5). Aunt Crystal asked for a copy of the low chart. Wren sings in the youth choir at Little Zion Freewill Baptist; Dr. Varghese's office trained the choir leader. Mr. Slone will send the plan to the bus garage.

title: OT Evaluation - Caudill-Fields (fictional test record)
text:
CANEY COUNTY PUBLIC SCHOOLS - Office of Special Education
OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY EVALUATION REPORT - CONFIDENTIAL

STUDENT: CAUDILL-FIELDS, SCOUT E.   Case No.: OT-26-0415-SCF
DOB: 03/14/2019   CA at testing: 7 yrs 5 mos   Grade: 2   Sex: F
SSID: 4417820391   Lunch #: 30672   Medicaid ID: 8812047735
School: Laurel Fork Elementary   Teacher: Mrs. Amber Whitaker (Rm 12)
Parent/Guardian: Tiffany Fields (mother); Darrell Sturgill (stepdad)
Address: 2280 Left Fork of Lick Branch Rd., up Sturgill Holler
         Mailing: RR 3 Box 118-A, Laurel Gap, KY 41766
Home: (606) 555-0143   Mom cell: 606-555-0178   tfields.mom@example.com
Referral: Aug. 27, 2026   Testing: 9/9/2026 and 9/11/26   Report: September 18, 2026
Evaluator: Kendra Slone, MOT, OTR/L   (606) 555-0190 ext. 214   kslone@example.org

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Scout Elaine Caudill-Fields ("Scouty" at home) was referred by the ARC at the request of her mother and teacher. Mrs. Whitaker reports Scout's written work is "hard for anybody to read, including Scout," that she avoids copying from the board, and that she melts down during fire drills, assemblies, and cafeteria lunch. Scout has received Tier 2 fine motor support at LFE since August 2025, when the family moved back from Dayton to live near her mamaw and papaw. Progress monitoring (per A.W. classroom log) shows limited gains.

BACKGROUND / HEALTH
Per parent interview (9/9/2026) and records from Big Laurel Pediatrics, Scout was born at 35 weeks with a 9-day NICU stay. Her pediatrician, Dr. Priya Raman, notes recurrent ear infections with PE tubes at age 2; hearing within normal limits 04/2026. Scout is left-handed; Mamaw (Loretta "Retta" Caudill) reports she switched hands until about age 5. Scout has a twin brother, Colt, in the other 2nd-grade section at LFE; per Ms. Fields, Colt "never had any of this trouble."

Scout lives with her mother, stepdad, and Colt. Mr. Sturgill runs Sturgill's Tire & Lube on Hwy 7, and Scout spends most afternoons there or at Mamaw Retta's across the creek. Papaw Everett Caudill raises bantam chickens, and Scout shows them with the Caney County 4-H Cloverbuds; she was the only first grader to place at the county fair poultry show. The family attends Lick Branch Freewill Baptist, where Aunt Shawna teaches her Sunday school class and says Scout "chews her sleeves raw" during singing.

TEACHER REPORT
Mrs. Whitaker describes a bright, verbal student; i-Ready Reading places her on grade level (scale score 487). Written output is the main concern: she needs 2-3 times longer than peers to finish a journal entry and erases until the paper tears. She covers her ears in the cafeteria and gym; Coach Randall Adams lets her warm up at the edge of the floor. She seeks deep pressure (crawls under the reading table).

PARENT REPORT
Mornings are hard: refuses tags, jeans, and socks with seams. Buttons and zippers still hard. Loves swinging and climbing hay bales at Papaw Ev's barn.

ASSESSMENTS ADMINISTERED
BOT-2, fine motor composites; Beery VMI, 6th Ed., with supplemental tests;
Sensory Profile 2 (Caregiver and School Companion); handwriting sample; interviews

BOT-2 (scale score M=15, SD=5; standard score M=50, SD=10)
Fine Motor Precision ........ scale score 9
Fine Motor Integration ...... scale score 10
Fine Manual Control ......... standard score 37, 10th %ile, Below Average
Manual Dexterity ............ scale score 8
Upper-Limb Coordination ..... scale score 13
Manual Coordination ......... standard score 41, 18th %ile, Average (low end)

Scout's Fine Manual Control standard score of 37 (10th percentile) falls in the Below Average range.

BEERY VMI (standard score M=100, SD=15)
Visual-Motor Integration ..... SS 78, 7th %ile, Low
Visual Perception ............ SS 94, 34th %ile, Average
Motor Coordination ........... SS 72, 3rd %ile, Low

The gap between Visual Perception and Motor Coordination points to motor execution, not visual processing.

SENSORY PROFILE 2 (Caregiver: Ms. Fields; School Companion: Mrs. Whitaker)
Seeking .............. raw 58, More Than Others
Avoiding ............. raw 34, Just Like the Majority of Others
Sensitivity .......... raw 52, More Than Others
Registration ......... raw 61, Much More Than Others
Touch section ........ Much More Than Others
Auditory section ..... Much More Than Others
School Factor 3 (Tolerance) ..... Much More Than Others

HANDWRITING SAMPLE
Near-point copy of a 3-line sentence: 14 letters per minute; 58% of words legible to an unfamiliar reader. Static quadrupod grip with thumb wrap and heavy pressure (indentations through 3 sheets). Reversals of b/d in 4 of 9 opportunities; inconsistent letter size; no spacing between words. She wrote "SCOUT F." at the top, then asked to stop.

SUMMARY
Fine motor and visual-motor deficits plus sensory processing differences (touch/auditory over-responsivity, low registration) interfere with written output and participation in noisy settings. OT is recommended as a related service.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Direct OT: 60 minutes per week (2 x 30-minute sessions), pull-out.
2. OT consultation with classroom teacher: 20 minutes per month.
3. Sensory diet: movement break every 20-30 minutes; heavy work jobs.
Accommodations: pencil grip and slant board for all written tasks; near-point copy instead of copying from the board; extended time (1.5x) on written assignments; noise-reducing headphones during assemblies and fire drills; wobble cushion.
Proposed goals:
- will copy a 3-line sentence from near point with 80% legibility in 4 of 5 trials
- will use a self-regulation strategy to remain in a noisy setting for 15 minutes in 4 of 5 opportunities

Results to be reviewed at the ARC meeting Oct. 6, 2026 at LFE.

text:
Tolliver County Schools - Office of Special Education Services
Phone (606) 555-0192 ext. 214

THREE-YEAR RE-EVALUATION SUMMARY / REVIEW OF EXISTING DATA
CONFIDENTIAL - FERPA / 707 KAR 1:360

STUDENT: FIELDS, COLTON WAYNE        Case #: RE-2026-TC-0417
DOB: 03/17/2012   Age: 14-6   Grade: 8
SSID: 2011804473   Lunch #: 40917   Medicaid ID: 9187245630

Address: 4471 Left Fork of Brushy Creek Rd., up Tackett Holler
Mail: RR 2 Box 118-A, Laurel Gap, KY 41788
Home (606) 555-0147 / Mom cell 606-555-0163 / tessa.gayheartfields@example.com
Case Manager: Mrs. Jolene Pennington, jpennington@example.org
ARC Meeting: Oct. 6, 2026   Last Re-eval: 10/19/2023   Initial: April 2017 (Beech Bottom Elementary)

I. REASON FOR RE-EVALUATION
Colton ("Colt" at school, "Bubba" at home) is due for his three-year re-evaluation. At the planning ARC on 9-2-26 the committee reviewed existing data and requested new cognitive, adaptive and language testing. Consent signed 09/03/2026.

II. REVIEW OF EXISTING DATA
Source                Date         Result
Vision/Hearing        08/21/2026   Passed both
Medical update        August 2025  No new dx; seasonal allergies
i-Ready Reading       09/08/2026   441, Grade 2 placement

KSA Grade 7           May 2026     Reading Novice / Math Novice
Attendance 2025-26                 9 absences
Discipline                         0 referrals

Medical update is from Dr. Anil Varghese at Three Forks Family Medicine. Records show C.W.F. was placed with a foster mom, Wanda Pratt, for four months and returned home Nov. 2021; DCBS Case No. TC-21-DN-0388 is closed. He lives with his mother, stepdad and mamaw. Fall i-Ready Reading scale score of 441 (Grade 2 placement) is unchanged from last spring.

III. COGNITIVE / ACHIEVEMENT
WJ-IV COG and ACH given 9/14/2026 and 9/16/2026 by Lacey Bowling, Ed.S., School Psychologist.

Cluster                        SS   %ile  Range
General Intellectual Ability   58   0.3   Very Low
Comprehension-Knowledge        62   1     Very Low
Fluid Reasoning                61   0.5   Very Low
Short-Term Working Memory      66   1     Very Low
Broad Reading                  64   1     Very Low
Broad Mathematics              61   0.5   Very Low
Broad Written Language         67   1     Very Low
Basic Reading Skills           70   2     Low

Colton earned a GIA standard score of 58 (0.3 percentile), consistent with his prior GIA of 60. His relative strength is Basic Reading Skills (SS 70); he decodes CVC and CVCe words but loses meaning above a second-grade passage. He knows math facts only for 2s, 5s and 10s.

IV. ADAPTIVE BEHAVIOR
Vineland-3: Parent/Caregiver Form (mother and mamaw), Teacher Rating Form (Mrs. Pennington).
Domain                  Parent SS  Teacher SS
Communication           66         60
Daily Living Skills     78         70
Socialization           69         64
ABC                     68         63

Vineland-3 Adaptive Behavior Composite of 68 (parent) and 63 (teacher) are both Low. The family has a small cow-calf operation and raises burley tobacco on Papaw Delmer's place. Tessa and Mamaw (Loretta Fields) report that Colt feeds the cattle before the bus, bottle-feeds calves, drives the side-by-side with supervision, and knows each cow by her tag number. He still needs reminders to shower, cannot count change from a $5 bill, and does not know his own phone number or address. He sings and plays the mandolin with his mamaw at Little Zion Freewill Baptist Church. Aunt Crystal (Crystal Amburgey), who keeps him weekends, agreed. Mr. Sturgill drives a coal truck for Big Laurel Hauling; his mother is a CNA at Hillview Nursing and Rehab.

V. SPEECH-LANGUAGE (Mrs. Angela Stidham, CCC-SLP)
CELF-5 Core Language Score 61 (0.5 percentile); Receptive Language Index 64; Expressive Language Index 60. Colton's sentences are short and he has trouble sequencing steps.

VI. TEACHER INPUT
Mrs. Pennington (resource reading/math): "Colt is the hardest worker in my room. He needs one- or two-step directions and a picture checklist."
Mr. Travis Hall (science, collaborative): Needs guided notes and word banks. In Mr. Hall's ag-science unit he was the only student to bring a calf to school.
Coach Wells (PE / archery): Made the CFMS archery team last spring and scored 241 at the regional tournament; upset by unannounced schedule changes.
Ms. Kristy Slone (social studies): Answers orally at about 70% accuracy with 3 answer choices when tests are read aloud.

VII. ARC DECISIONS (Oct. 6, 2026)
1. Continues eligible under Mild Mental Disability with secondary Speech/Language Impairment.
2. SDI in reading 250 minutes per week and math 250 minutes per week (resource); collaborative services in science and social studies 225 minutes per week; speech-language therapy 60 minutes per week.
3. Accommodations: extended time (1.5x) on classwork and tests; tests read aloud except for reading comprehension; calculator; reduced answer choices (3); guided notes.
4. Goals: Given a grade 3 passage, will read 80 words correct per minute with 95% accuracy; will count back change from $1, $5, and $10 in 4 of 5 trials; will state home address and phone number in 4 of 5 trials; will use a picture checklist to complete a 3-step routine independently.
5. Transition planning begins at 14. He wants to "work cattle like Papaw" and shows a Hereford heifer with the Tolliver County 4-H Livestock Club.
6. ESY not warranted. Regular KSA with accommodations.

Home: (606) 555-0148     Mamaw cell: 606-555-0192

FAMILY ROUTINES AND BACKGROUND
Journey (called "Jo-Jo" at home) has lived with her mamaw and papaw since May 2024, following a short foster placement with foster mom Mrs. Darlene Ritchie that began in March 2024. Her mother, Kayla Fields-Slone, lives out of state and visits about every other weekend with her husband Cody Slone, whom Journey calls her stepdad. Aunt Tammy (Tammy Gayheart) keeps Journey on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons at her home daycare. Mamaw Retta is a cafeteria cook at LME, so Journey rides in with her at 6:30 a.m. and is the only Head Start student who eats breakfast with the cooks. Papaw Delmer is retired from the Stony Fork No. 7 mine and runs a small-engine repair shop out of his garage; Journey "helps" him. She feeds Papaw's coonhounds every evening, goes to Tiny Tumblers on Saturday mornings with Coach Mandy Pratt, and tags along to Cloverbuds 4-H with a cousin. The family attends Little Rockhouse Freewill Baptist Church, where Journey stands on the pew to sing during Sunday night singing. She is daytime toilet trained and wears a pull-up at night. Mrs. Fields reports picky eating and 20-30 minute meltdowns when routines change after weekend visits.

FIRST STEPS AND TRANSITION HISTORY
Journey was referred to First Steps on Oct. 18, 2023 (age 19 months) by Dr. Lena Holbrook, Redbud Hollow Pediatrics, for no words and limited gestures. She received weekly developmental intervention home visits from Mr. Wade Couch, DI, and speech therapy twice monthly; service coordinator was Ms. Tonya Gibson. Services paused during foster care, resumed June 2024. The transition conference was held 12/09/2024 with preschool coordinator Mr. Travis Pigman. J.R.F. exited First Steps 3/26/25 and received itinerant home-based preschool services (SLP home visits twice monthly) from April 2025 through May 2026. Guardians chose a Head Start classroom starting August 2026. Dr. Holbrook's 07/11/2026 well-child note reports normal hearing and amblyopia patching; Journey is the only child in her class wearing an eye patch.

HOME VISITS
Home visit 08/14/2026 (Ms. Carla Sturgill, Family Advocate; Mrs. Rebecca Holcomb, CCC-SLP) and 9-8-26 (Mrs. Brandi Noble, teacher). Journey led staff to the coonhound pen, said "dog out" and "Papaw fix," and followed Mamaw's routine directions with gestures. Papaw's concern: "Folks outside the family can't understand her."

ASSESSMENT RESULTS
Battelle Developmental Inventory, Third Edition (BDI-3), given 09/03/2026 and 09/08/2026 by Mrs. Holcomb and Mrs. Noble (mean 100, SD 15):

Domain              DQ    %ile   Range
Adaptive            78    7      Below Average
Personal-Social     84    14     Below Average
Communication       68    2      Delayed
Motor               88    21     Low Average
Cognitive           76    5      Below Average
BDI-3 Total         74    4      Delayed

Journey's BDI-3 Total DQ of 74 (4th percentile) and Communication DQ of 68 (2nd percentile) meet state DD criteria (2 SD below the mean in one area); Cognitive is also more than 1.5 SD below the mean.

Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), 09/10/2026:
  Auditory Comprehension SS 71, 3rd percentile
  Expressive Communication SS 64, 1st percentile
  Total Language SS 66, 1st percentile
GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words standard score of 62 (below 1st percentile). Vineland-3 Parent/Caregiver Form (completed by Mamaw): Adaptive Behavior Composite of 76 (5th percentile); Communication 70, Daily Living Skills 79, Socialization 81. ASQ:SE-2 score of 75 falls in the monitoring zone.

Communication: About 40 single words and 5-8 two-word combinations ("more juice," "Mamaw go"). Intelligibility is about 40% to unfamiliar listeners; she deletes final consonants and fronts velars ("tootie" for cookie). Follows 1-step directions with gestures in 3 of 5 trials.
Cognitive/Pre-academic: Matches 4 colors, rote counts to 5, identifies circle and square.
Motor: Runs and climbs; palmar grasp on crayons; OT consult for fine motor.
Social/Adaptive: Parallel play; 3-4 transition meltdowns daily in week one, now 1-2 with a first-then board.

IMPACT: Delays in communication and cognition limit Journey's participation in circle time, peer play, and classroom routines at LME.

PROPOSED SERVICES
Speech-language therapy 60 minutes per week (2 x 30 min), push-in and pull-out
Specially designed instruction 150 minutes per week in the Head Start classroom
OT consultation 30 minutes per month

DRAFT GOAL: Given a visual choice board and a verbal model, Journey will use 2- to 3-word phrases to request, comment, or protest in 4 of 5 opportunities across 3 consecutive data days.

ACCOMMODATIONS: visual schedule with photo cards; extended wait time of 5-7 seconds; first-then board at transitions; preferential seating near the adult during circle time.
